title: Jacob, Israel, and Ephraim
notes: The chapter builds a tight, law-positive chain from Jacob’s crooked heart through Israel’s straightening to Ephraim’s fruit-in-affliction and the two sticks/olive trees, with dense, well-chosen scripture and no hedging. The dual-name argument against the old-man/new-man swap is clear and forceful. Issues are localized: one factual timing slip that attaches “the very night” to Genesis 35:10, two author-prose sentences that open with And, mild presenter staging in the “See when” and closing “Hold on” lines, and a stranded citation that breaks the John 1:47 sentence. No AI vocabulary, doctrine invention, or scripture-quote corruption appears.

proposals.old: The very night the name is given, God says __“thy name shall not be called any more Jacob”__ (Genesis 35:10) — and then keeps right on calling him Jacob, and names Himself to the end __“the God of Jacob.”__
proposals.new: Even after the name is given, God says __“thy name shall not be called any more Jacob”__ (Genesis 35:10) — and then keeps right on calling him Jacob, and names Himself to the end __“the God of Jacob.”__
proposals.summary: Remove false claim that Genesis 35:10 occurs the night the name is given.
proposals.rationale: The name is first given at the ford (Genesis 32:28); Genesis 35:10 is the later Bethel reaffirmation. The dual-naming point stands without the erroneous “very night” timing.

proposals.old: And the very root that named him crooked names the cure — __“the _crooked_ [_aqob_] shall be made straight”__ (Isaiah 40:4).
proposals.new: The very root that named him crooked names the cure — __“the _crooked_ [_aqob_] shall be made straight”__ (Isaiah 40:4).
proposals.summary: Drop sentence-initial And in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And/But/That at the start of author sentences. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim and the parallel intact.

proposals.new: The name is won at dawn.
proposals.summary: Replace presenter cue with a direct assertion.
proposals.rationale: “See when” functions as a director cue. The replacement states the same timing claim without staging language.

proposals.old: Hold on through the night, and the morning brings the new name, the renewed covenant, joy, and life.
proposals.new: The one who holds on through the night receives the new name, the renewed covenant, joy, and life in the morning.
proposals.summary: Convert closing imperative into an assertion of the pattern.
proposals.rationale: The line is a reader-directed charge. Restating it as the pattern already established keeps the density and removes the staging tone.

proposals.old: And Paul names the harvest in the very words of the blessing — __“the fulness of the Gentiles”__ (Romans 11:25): _melo ha-goyim_, come in at last.
proposals.new: Paul names the harvest in the very words of the blessing — __“the fulness of the Gentiles”__ (Romans 11:25): _melo ha-goyim_, come in at last.
proposals.summary: Drop sentence-initial And in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids And at the start of author sentences. The claim and the Hebrew link remain unchanged.

proposals.old:
The end of the work is a man with the grasping gone, and Jesus names him the moment He sees him: __“Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!”__
(John 1:47) — Jacob, with the Jacob taken out.
proposals.new: The end of the work is a man with the grasping gone, and Jesus names him the moment He sees him: __“Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!”__ (John 1:47) — Jacob, with the Jacob taken out.
proposals.summary: Pull the stranded citation onto the same line as the quote.
proposals.rationale: The reference currently sits alone on the next line, breaking the sentence. Keeping citation with the quote matches the chapter’s other inline references.
